atoms.text: Aoife now wants to take you to see Northern Ireland’s landscapes. Will you go around the countryside with her?

instruction.text: Aoife wants to know if you recognise what Northern Irish landscapes look like. Select the images of landscapes in Northern Ireland.

feedback.end: Northern Ireland is made up of lots of hills and low mountains. There are many stretches of beautiful coastline to walk along too!
feedback.wrong: This is Mount Everest in Asia. Northern Ireland doesn’t have mountains that are this high and snowy.

instruction.text: Aoife asks if you know the names of landscapes you might see around Northern Ireland. Drag the images to the correct words.
Aoife has marked three famous natural areas in Northern Ireland on her map. Find the Giant’s Causeway on the map to visit it.
This is the Giant’s Causeway. Find the sea in the image to learn more.

end.text: The Giant’s Causeway is a coast made up of 40,000 rocky columns. These were formed from a volcanic eruption over 50 million years ago!

instruction.text: Find Lough Neagh on the map to visit it.
This is Lough Neagh. Find the clouds in the image to learn more.

feedback.end: Lough Neagh is the largest lake in the whole UK. Almost half of Northern Ireland’s drinking water comes from here.

instruction.text: Find the Marble Arch Caves on the map to visit them.
These are the Marble Arch Caves. Find the walkway in the image to learn more.

end.text: These caves were formed over 300 million years ago. They make up the longest cave system in Northern Ireland.
